problem_statement: TailGrids play-astro is a runnable multi-page Astro marketing template (Home, About, Pricing, Team, Contact, Blog collection, Sign In, Sign Up) with a shared header/footer, dark-mode toggle, the PLAY blue-and-white visual system (bright blue #3758F9 hero and CTA bands, green #13C296 secondary accent, white rounded cards, dark navy #090E34 footer). The site is being positioned as an AI launch readiness service for teams preparing AI workflow pilots. The PRD asks you to add a site-wide 'Launch readiness track' rail, rendered ONCE by the shared footer so it appears at the top of the footer on every marketing surface (home, pricing, blog and contact). The rail is an on-brand PLAY card (white surface, blue accent title, green secondary toggle) with a row of five launch-milestone chips (Discovery, Workflow Map, AI Pilot, Security Review, Launch Review) and their hints, a 'Now tracking' cohort readout, and a 'Switch cohort' control that flips the rail between the discovery and pilot cohorts and keeps the readout in sync. A previous revision shipped this rail but (a) pinned the chip row to a fixed-width no-wrap track that overflows a 390px phone horizontally, (b) styled it as a plain gray slab instead of the PLAY card surface, and (c) only rendered it on the home page. Rework the launch-readiness rail so it: lays out responsively with no horizontal overflow on mobile; keeps the PLAY blue-and-white card styling; renders consistently across home, pricing, blog and contact; and keeps the Switch cohort control wired so the readout always reflects the active cohort after a click. Keep the milestone chips, their labels, their hints, and the footer/header/route structure exactly as shipped; the fix must live in the launch-readiness rail component's own file.
required_content: The site-wide launch-readiness rail renders on the home, pricing, blog and contact surfaces (rendered once by the shared footer) with all five launch-milestone chips (Discovery, Workflow Map, AI Pilot, Security Review, Launch Review) and their descriptive hints.
On a 390px mobile view the milestone row lays out without any horizontal document overflow (no horizontal scrollbar).
The rail keeps the PLAY blue-and-white card surface: white background, blue #3758F9 accent title, rounded chips, green secondary 'Switch cohort' control, matching the surrounding footer chrome.
The 'Switch cohort' control flips the rail between the discovery and pilot cohorts and re-syncs the 'Now tracking' readout so it reflects the active cohort after each click.
Header navigation, dark-mode toggle, pricing cards, blog collection routing, and the contact form fields remain present and the site builds with the existing Astro pipeline.
design_constraints: Preserve the PLAY/TailGrids visual language: blue #3758F9 hero and CTA bands, green #13C296 secondary accent, white rounded cards, light gray section bands, dark navy footer, and the existing dark-mode toggle.
Keep the launch-milestone chips' content, labels, and hint text identical; only the rail's responsive layout, surface styling, cross-page presence and cohort wiring may change.
The change must live in the launch-readiness rail component's own file; do not alter the header, pricing section, blog collection, contact form, or other page bodies.
The milestone row must wrap or otherwise reflow so a 390px viewport shows no horizontal overflow, while the desktop and tablet layouts stay visually stable.
Do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, analytics, or network calls; every page must stay runtime-clean (no console or network errors).
state_constraints: desktop_rail_home and desktop_rail_pricing capture the launch-readiness rail at 1440px, where the rail sits at the top of the footer on the PLAY white card surface and lays out without overflow on every leg.

mobile_home and mobile_rail_home capture the rail at 390px: on the shipped (defective) revision the fixed-width no-wrap milestone row pushes the document past the viewport, causing a horizontal-scroll defect that the fix must remove.

desktop_rail_home, desktop_rail_pricing, desktop_rail_blog and desktop_rail_contact all carry the shared launch-readiness rail in the reference; the rail must be present on each of these four routes (cross-page consistency).
launch_focus_toggle clicks the Switch cohort control on the home rail; after the click the 'Now tracking' readout must read 'pilot cohort' (the readout re-syncs to the active cohort).

Source inspection confirms the footer is rendered by the shared Layout on every route, so a single rail instance placed in the footer covers the whole site; the rail reuses the PLAY blue/green palette from tailwind.config.cjs.

change_completion: The launch-readiness rail renders across home, pricing, blog and contact with all five milestone chips and their hints.
The Switch cohort control re-syncs the 'Now tracking' readout after a click so the terminal state reflects the active cohort.
The mobile launch rail shows no horizontal overflow after the fix.
design_consistency: The rail keeps the PLAY white card surface, rounded chips, blue accent title and green secondary control on every route.
Desktop and tablet layouts stay visually stable; only the mobile reflow changes.
regression: Header navigation, dark-mode toggle, pricing cards, blog collection routing and the contact form remain reachable and unchanged, and the build succeeds with the existing Astro pipeline.
Every page stays runtime-clean with no console or network errors.
responsive: 390px mobile launch rail has no horizontal document overflow.
The launch-milestone chips wrap intentionally on narrow viewports rather than forcing a fixed-width horizontal track.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro (TailGrids play-astro PLAY template) cross-page experience continuity task, hardened to L4. The reference ships a responsive, on-brand PLAY 'Launch readiness track' rail rendered site-wide by the shared footer, with a wired Switch-cohort control. Content and DOM are byte-identical across the reference, the shipped-with-defect baseline and a shallow non-fix bad solution; only the launch-readiness rail component's file differs. The bad solution fails four orthogonal product gates: no_horizontal_overflow (mobile milestone-row overflow), visual_regression (off-palette dark-teal slab vs the white/blue PLAY card), cross-page dom_assertions (rail missing on the blog and contact routes), and interaction_assertions (Switch cohort click succeeds but the readout stays stale). The baseline reproduces the original three layout/visual/presence defects but keeps the cohort wiring correct, so it fails the first three gates and passes the interaction gate. Local hero/logo/blog assets and the PLAY palette are reused; no remote fonts or stock imagery. Product-grade gates: enforce_console_errors (max 0), cross-page DOM assertions, visual_regression on in-viewport rail states, and an interaction-trajectory terminal-state assertion.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: play-astro is a runnable multi-page Astro PLAY marketing template (home, pricing, blog collection, contact) with a shared footer rendered on every route; experience_continuity adds a responsive, site-wide launch-readiness rail through that footer, anchored on four orthogonal product gates (overflow, visual, cross-page presence, interaction terminal state).
